questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the proportionality between (I) Bond length and size of atom (II) Bond length and multiplicity of bond respectively?
questions.solution:
Bond length is the equilibrium distance between the nuclei of two bonded atoms in a molecule.

As the size of the bonded atoms increases, the distance between their nuclei increases. Thus, bond length is directly proportional to the size of the atom.

Bond multiplicity refers to the number of bonds between two atoms (single, double, triple). As bond multiplicity increases, the bond becomes stronger and the atoms are pulled closer together, decreasing the bond length. Thus, bond length is inversely proportional to the multiplicity of the bond.

Hence, (I) is direct and (II) is inverse.

Answer: (I)- direct (II)- inverse

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify linear molecule from following.
questions.solution:
For $\text{SO}_2$, the central sulphur atom has $2$ bond pairs and $1$ lone pair. The hybridization is $sp^2$ and the shape is bent.

For $\text{BCl}_3$, the central boron atom has $3$ bond pairs and $0$ lone pairs. The hybridization is $sp^2$ and the shape is trigonal planar.

For $\text{CO}_2$, the central carbon atom has $2$ bond pairs (sigma bonds) and $0$ lone pairs. The hybridization is $sp$ and the shape is linear.

For $\text{NH}_3$, the central nitrogen atom has $3$ bond pairs and $1$ lone pair. The hybridization is $sp^3$ and the shape is trigonal pyramidal.

Thus, $\text{CO}_2$ is the only linear molecule among the given options.

Answer: $\text{CO}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following gases is least soluble in water under same conditions of temperature and pressure ?
questions.solution:
Water is a polar solvent. Gases that are polar, can form hydrogen bonds, or react with water are highly soluble in it.

$\text{HCl}$ and $\text{NH}_3$ are highly soluble due to ionization and hydrogen bonding, respectively.

$\text{CO}_2$ is moderately soluble as it reacts with water to form carbonic acid.

$\text{O}_2$ is a non-polar gas and interacts with water only through weak dipole-induced dipole forces, making it the least soluble among the given gases.

Answer: $\text{O}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which is the correct decreasing order of boiling points for different compounds from following ?
questions.solution:
The boiling point of haloalkanes increases with an increase in the molecular mass and the size of the halogen atom due to the stronger van der Waals forces of attraction.

Comparing the given compounds:
$\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$ has one chlorine atom.
$\text{CH}_3\text{Br}$ has one bromine atom, which is heavier and larger than chlorine.
$\text{CH}_2\text{Br}_2$ has two bromine atoms.
$\text{CHBr}_3$ has three bromine atoms.

The molecular mass follows the order: $\text{CHBr}_3 \gt \text{CH}_2\text{Br}_2 \gt \text{CH}_3\text{Br} \gt \text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$.

Therefore, the decreasing order of boiling points is $\text{CHBr}_3 \gt \text{CH}_2\text{Br}_2 \gt \text{CH}_3\text{Br} \gt \text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$.

Answer: $\text{CHBr}_3 \gt \text{CH}_2\text{Br}_2 \gt \text{CH}_3\text{Br} \gt \text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is favourable condition for the formation of ionic bond ?
options: Low ionization enthalpy of metal and low negative value of electron gain enthalpy of non metal.
Low ionization enthalpy of metal and high negative value of electron gain enthalpy of non metal.
High ionization enthalpy of metal and high negative value of electron gain enthalpy of non metal.
High ionization enthalpy of metal and low negative value of electron gain enthalpy of non metal.
questions.solution:
The formation of an ionic bond involves the transfer of electrons from a metal atom to a non-metal atom.

The metal atom loses an electron to form a cation. This process requires energy, which is the ionization enthalpy. A lower ionization enthalpy means the metal can easily lose its valence electrons, favoring cation formation.

The non-metal atom gains an electron to form an anion. This process releases energy, which is measured as the electron gain enthalpy. A high negative value of electron gain enthalpy indicates that a large amount of energy is released, making the formation of the anion highly favorable.

Therefore, the favorable conditions for the formation of an ionic bond are a low ionization enthalpy of the metal and a high negative value of electron gain enthalpy of the non-metal.

Answer: Low ionization enthalpy of metal and high negative value of electron gain enthalpy of non metal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of bond pair of electrons and lone pair of electrons present in the valence shell of chalcogens in their hydride ?
options: 2 - Bond pair and 1- lone pair of electrons
2 - Bond pair and 2- lone pair of electrons
3 - Bond pair and 1- lone pair of electrons
3 - Bond pair and 2- lone pair of electrons
questions.solution:
Chalcogens belong to Group 16 of the periodic table and have 6 valence electrons ($ns^2 np^4$).

The general formula for the hydrides of chalcogens is $H_2E$ (where $E = O, S, Se, Te, Po$).

In the formation of $H_2E$, the chalcogen atom shares two of its valence electrons with two hydrogen atoms to form two single covalent bonds. This results in 2 bond pairs of electrons.

The remaining 4 valence electrons on the chalcogen atom do not participate in bonding and exist as 2 lone pairs of electrons.

Thus, the valence shell of a chalcogen in its hydride contains 2 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs of electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of $sp^3$ hybrid carbon atoms in $\text{HO}(\text{CH}_2)_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$?
questions.solution:
The given molecule is 3-methylbutan-1-ol, with the expanded structural formula $\text{HO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$.

In this structure, every carbon atom is bonded to four other atoms (either carbon, hydrogen, or oxygen) entirely through single ($\sigma$) bonds.

Since there are no $\pi$ bonds present, all the carbon atoms are $sp^3$ hybridized.

Counting the carbon atoms:
Two $-\text{CH}_2-$ groups $\rightarrow 2$ carbon atoms
One $-\text{CH}-$ group $\rightarrow 1$ carbon atom
Two $-\text{CH}_3$ groups $\rightarrow 2$ carbon atoms

Total number of $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atoms $= 2 + 1 + 2 = 5$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify correct order for repulsion between electron pair present in valence shell of central atom of molecule?
questions.solution:
According to VSEPR theory, the electron pairs in the valence shell of the central atom repel each other to minimize electron-electron repulsion.

Lone pairs (Lp) are localized on the central atom and are attracted by only one nucleus, so they occupy more space and exert greater repulsion.

Bond pairs (Bp) are shared between two atoms and are attracted by two nuclei, so they occupy less space and exert lesser repulsion.

Thus, the correct order of repulsion between electron pairs is $\text{Lp-Lp} \gt \text{Lp-Bp} \gt \text{Bp-Bp}$.

Answer: $\text{Lp-Lp} \gt \text{Lp-Bp} \gt \text{Bp-Bp}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following molecule exhibits paramagnetism?
questions.solution:
According to Molecular Orbital Theory, the electronic configuration of $\text{O}_2$ (16 electrons) is:

${\sigma_{1s}}^2 {{\sigma^{*}}_{1s}}^2 \sigma_{2s}^2 {{\sigma^{*}}_{2s}}^2 {\sigma_{2p_z}}^2 {\pi_{2p_x}}^2 {\pi_{2p_y}}^2 {{\pi^{*}}_{2p_x}}^1 {{\pi^{*}}_{2p_y}}^1$

Due to the presence of two unpaired electrons in the degenerate antibonding $\pi^{*}$ molecular orbitals, $\text{O}_2$ is paramagnetic.

$\text{N}_2$ (14 electrons) and $\text{F}_2$ (18 electrons) have all their electrons paired in their molecular orbitals, making them diamagnetic.

$\text{O}_3$ (ozone) also has all its electrons paired and is diamagnetic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following ethers is gaseous at room temperature ?
questions.solution:
Dimethyl ether and ethyl methyl ether (methoxyethane) are gases at room temperature.

Other lower homologues of ethers, such as diethyl ether (ethoxyethane), 1-methoxypropane, and 1-ethoxypropane, are colourless, highly volatile liquids at room temperature.

Therefore, methoxyethane is gaseous at room temperature.

Answer: Methoxyethane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following gases is least soluble in water at same temperature and pressure ?
questions.solution:
Solubility of a gas in water depends on its ability to interact with water molecules. Water is a polar solvent.

$\text{NH}_3$ is highly soluble in water due to its ability to form intermolecular hydrogen bonds with water.

$\text{HCl}$ is a polar molecule that ionizes completely in water, making it highly soluble.

$\text{CO}_2$ is moderately soluble because it reacts with water to form carbonic acid ($\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$).

$\text{N}_2$ is a non-polar diatomic gas that neither reacts with water nor forms hydrogen bonds. Therefore, it has the weakest interaction with water molecules and is the least soluble among the given gases.

Answer: $\text{N}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Select the incorrect statement from the following.
options: In $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{NF}_3$ the orbital dipole due to lone pair is in the same direction as that of resultant dipole moment of other three bonds
Dipole moment of $\text{NH}_3$ is greater than $\text{NF}_3$
questions.solution:
Both $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{NF}_3$ have a central nitrogen atom with $sp^3$ hybridization and one lone pair, giving them a trigonal pyramidal shape. Both are polar molecules.

In $\text{NH}_3$, nitrogen is more electronegative than hydrogen. The bond dipole moments of the three N-H bonds are directed towards the nitrogen atom. Their resultant dipole moment is in the same direction as the orbital dipole due to the lone pair, leading to a higher net dipole moment.

In $\text{NF}_3$, fluorine is more electronegative than nitrogen. The bond dipole moments of the three N-F bonds are directed towards the fluorine atoms. Their resultant dipole moment is in the opposite direction to the orbital dipole due to the lone pair. This partial cancellation results in a lower net dipole moment for $\text{NF}_3$ compared to $\text{NH}_3$.

Therefore, the statement that the orbital dipole due to the lone pair is in the same direction as the resultant dipole moment of the three bonds in both molecules is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following metal halides have more covalent character?
questions.solution:
According to Fajan's rules, the covalent character of a metal halide increases with an increase in the positive charge on the central metal cation. A higher charge on the cation results in greater polarizing power, which increases the covalent character of the bond.

The oxidation states of the central metal cations in the given options are:
$\text{SnCl}_2$: $+2$
$\text{PbCl}_4$: $+4$
$\text{SbCl}_3$: $+3$
$\text{PbCl}_2$: $+2$

Since $\text{Pb}$ in $\text{PbCl}_4$ has the highest oxidation state of $+4$, the $\text{Pb}^{4+}$ ion has the maximum polarizing power. Thus, $\text{PbCl}_4$ has the most covalent character.

Answer: $\text{PbCl}_4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compound has square pyramidal structure?
questions.solution:
The shape of the molecules can be determined using VSEPR theory by calculating the number of bond pairs (bp) and lone pairs (lp) on the central Xenon (Xe) atom, which has 8 valence electrons.

For $\text{XeF}_4$: Xe forms 4 single bonds with F atoms, using 4 electrons. Remaining electrons = 4 (2 lone pairs). With 4 bp and 2 lp, the hybridization is $sp^3d^2$ and the shape is square planar.

For $\text{XeF}_6$: Xe forms 6 single bonds with F atoms, using 6 electrons. Remaining electrons = 2 (1 lone pair). With 6 bp and 1 lp, the hybridization is $sp^3d^3$ and the shape is distorted octahedral.

For $\text{XeO}_3$: Xe forms 3 double bonds with O atoms, using 6 electrons. Remaining electrons = 2 (1 lone pair). With 3 bp ($\sigma$-bonds) and 1 lp, the hybridization is $sp^3$ and the shape is trigonal pyramidal.

For $\text{XeOF}_4$: Xe forms 1 double bond with O and 4 single bonds with F, using $2 + 4 = 6$ electrons. Remaining electrons = 2 (1 lone pair). With 5 bp ($\sigma$-bonds) and 1 lp, the hybridization is $sp^3d^2$ and the shape is square pyramidal.

Answer: $\text{XeOF}_4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is formal charge on sulphur in sulphuric acid molecule?
questions.solution:
The most stable Lewis structure of sulphuric acid ($H_2SO_4$) minimizes the formal charge by expanding the octet of the central sulphur atom. In this structure, sulphur forms two double bonds with two oxygen atoms and two single bonds with two hydroxyl ($-OH$) groups.

The formula for formal charge is:
Formal charge = (Valence electrons) - (Non-bonding electrons) - $\dfrac{1}{2}$ (Bonding electrons)

For the sulphur atom in $H_2SO_4$:
Number of valence electrons = $6$
Number of non-bonding electrons = $0$
Number of bonding electrons = $12$ (since it forms $6$ bonds)

Formal charge = $6 - 0 - \dfrac{12}{2} = 0$

Answer: $0$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the number of lone pair and bond pair electrons present in the valence shell of central atom in $\text{BrF}_3$.
options: 1 _ Lone pair and 2 _ Bond pair of electrons
2 _ Lone pair and 2 _ Bond pair of electrons
2 _ Lone pair and 3 _ Bond pair of electrons
1 _ Lone pair and 3 _ Bond pair of electrons
questions.solution:
The central atom in $\text{BrF}_3$ is Bromine ($\text{Br}$).

Number of valence electrons in $\text{Br} = 7$.

Bromine forms $3$ single bonds with $3$ Fluorine atoms. Therefore, the number of bond pairs is $3$.

Number of electrons used in bonding $= 3$.

Remaining valence electrons on the central atom $= 7 - 3 = 4$.

Number of lone pairs $= \dfrac{4}{2} = 2$.

Thus, the central atom has $2$ lone pairs and $3$ bond pairs of electrons.

Answer: 2 _ Lone pair and 3 _ Bond pair of electrons

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding Pi $(\pi)$ bond is NOT true ?
options: It is weaker than sigma bond.
It is formed by lateral overlapping of two half filled P orbitals.
It is formed after the formation of sigma bond.
The presence of Pi $(\pi)$ bond increases the bond length of covalent bond.
questions.solution:
A pi ($\pi$) bond is formed by the lateral or sideways overlapping of half-filled atomic orbitals (like p or d orbitals) after the formation of a sigma ($\sigma$) bond.

Because the extent of overlapping in a $\pi$ bond is less than that in a $\sigma$ bond, a $\pi$ bond is weaker than a $\sigma$ bond.

The presence of a $\pi$ bond between two atoms increases the bond order (e.g., from single to double or triple bond). An increase in bond order leads to a stronger attractive force between the atoms, which decreases the bond length. For example, the C-C single bond length is $1.54$ \AA, whereas the C=C double bond length is $1.34$ \AA.

Therefore, the statement that the presence of a $\pi$ bond increases the bond length is incorrect.

Answer: The presence of Pi $(\pi)$ bond increases the bond length of covalent bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify a molecule having highest dipole moment from following.
questions.solution:
The dipole moment of a molecule depends on its geometry and the electronegativity difference between its constituent atoms.

For $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, the oxygen atom is highly electronegative and possesses two lone pairs. The molecule has a bent structure, and the bond dipoles along with the lone pair dipoles reinforce each other, resulting in a high dipole moment of approximately $1.85\text{ D}$.

For $\text{NH}_3$, the nitrogen atom has one lone pair and the molecule is trigonal pyramidal. Its dipole moment is approximately $1.47\text{ D}$.

For $\text{CHCl}_3$, the molecule has a tetrahedral geometry but is asymmetric. Its dipole moment is approximately $1.04\text{ D}$.

For $\text{BeF}_2$, the molecule is linear and symmetric. The two $\text{Be-F}$ bond dipoles are equal and opposite, cancelling each other out and resulting in a dipole moment of $0\text{ D}$.

Thus, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ has the highest dipole moment among the given molecules.

Answer: $\text{H}_2\text{O}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the total number of electrons present in bonding and antibonding orbitals respectively in $\text{F}_2$ molecule according to MO theory ?
questions.solution:
The atomic number of fluorine ($\text{F}$) is $9$. Therefore, the total number of electrons in the $\text{F}_2$ molecule is $18$.

According to Molecular Orbital Theory, the electronic configuration of $\text{F}_2$ is:
$\sigma_{1s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{1s}{}^2 \sigma_{2s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{2s}{}^2 \sigma_{2p_z}^2 \pi_{2p_x}^2 \pi_{2p_y}^2 \pi^{*}_{2p_x}{}^2 \pi^{*}_{2p_y}{}^2$

The electrons present in orbitals without an asterisk are bonding electrons ($N_b$), and those in orbitals with an asterisk are antibonding electrons ($N_a$).

Number of bonding electrons ($N_b$) = $2 (\sigma_{1s}) + 2 (\sigma_{2s}) + 2 (\sigma_{2p_z}) + 2 (\pi_{2p_x}) + 2 (\pi_{2p_y}) = 10$

Number of antibonding electrons ($N_a$) = $2 (\sigma^{*}_{1s}) + 2 (\sigma^{*}_{2s}) + 2 (\pi^{*}_{2p_x}) + 2 (\pi^{*}_{2p_y}) = 8$

Thus, there are $10$ bonding electrons and $8$ antibonding electrons.

Answer: Bonding - 10, Antibonding - 8

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following molecules is paramagnetic?
questions.solution:
According to molecular orbital theory, the electronic configurations of the given molecules are written to determine the presence of unpaired electrons.

$\text{Li}_2$ ($6$ electrons): $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{1s}^{*2} \sigma_{2s}^{2}$

Since all electrons are paired, it is diamagnetic.

$\text{N}_2$ ($14$ electrons): $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{1s}^{*2} \sigma_{2s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{*2} \pi_{2p_x}^{2} \parallel \pi_{2p_y}^{2} \sigma_{2p_z}^{2}$

Since all electrons are paired, it is diamagnetic.

$\text{O}_2$ ($16$ electrons): $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{1s}^{*2} \sigma_{2s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{*2} \sigma_{2p_z}^{2} \pi_{2p_x}^{2} \parallel \pi_{2p_y}^{2} \pi_{2p_x}^{*1} \parallel \pi_{2p_y}^{*1}$

Due to the presence of two unpaired electrons in the $\pi^{*}$ antibonding molecular orbitals, $\text{O}_2$ is paramagnetic.

$\text{F}_2$ ($18$ electrons): $\sigma_{1s}^{2} \sigma_{1s}^{*2} \sigma_{2s}^{2} \sigma_{2s}^{*2} \sigma_{2p_z}^{2} \pi_{2p_x}^{2} \parallel \pi_{2p_y}^{2} \pi_{2p_x}^{*2} \parallel \pi_{2p_y}^{*2}$

Since all electrons are paired, it is diamagnetic.

Answer: $\text{O}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of bond and type of overlapping present in $\text{N}_2$ molecule ?
questions.solution:
The electronic configuration of a nitrogen atom is $1s^2 2s^2 2p^3$.

Each nitrogen atom has three half-filled $2p$ orbitals ($2p_x, 2p_y, 2p_z$). To achieve a stable octet configuration, two nitrogen atoms share three pairs of electrons, forming a triple bond ($N \equiv N$).

The triple bond consists of one $\sigma$ bond and two $\pi$ bonds. The $\sigma$ bond is formed by the axial overlapping of one set of $p$ orbitals (e.g., $2p_z - 2p_z$), while the two $\pi$ bonds are formed by the lateral overlapping of the remaining two sets of $p$ orbitals (e.g., $2p_x - 2p_x$ and $2p_y - 2p_y$).

Since all the orbitals involved in the bond formation are $p$ orbitals, the overlapping is of the p$-$p type.

Therefore, the $N_2$ molecule contains a triple bond and exhibits p$-$p overlap.

Answer: Triple bond and p$-$p overlap

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following order of dipole moment for stated molecules is correct?
questions.solution:
$\text{BF}_3$ has a symmetrical trigonal planar geometry, so its net dipole moment is zero.

In $\text{NH}_3$, the N-H bond dipoles and the lone pair dipole are in the same direction, which add up to give a high dipole moment.

In $\text{NF}_3$, the N-F bond dipoles and the lone pair dipole are in opposite directions, which partially cancel each other, resulting in a lower dipole moment than $\text{NH}_3$.

Therefore, the correct order of dipole moment is $\text{NH}_3 \gt \text{NF}_3 \gt \text{BF}_3$.

Answer: $\text{NH}_3 \gt \text{NF}_3 \gt \text{BF}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In the compound ${}^1\text{CH}_2 = {}^2\text{CH} - {}^3\text{CH}_2 - {}^4\text{CH}_2 - {}^5\text{C} \equiv {}^6\text{CH}$, The $C_2 - C_3$ bond is of type
questions.solution:
The given compound is $^{1}\text{CH}_2 = ^{2}\text{CH} - ^{3}\text{CH}_2 - ^{4}\text{CH}_2 - ^{5}\text{C} \equiv ^{6}\text{CH}$.

The hybridization of a carbon atom is determined by the number of sigma bonds it forms.

Carbon atom $C_2$ is bonded to one carbon atom via a double bond, one carbon atom via a single bond, and one hydrogen atom via a single bond. It forms $3$ sigma bonds and $1$ pi bond. Thus, $C_2$ is $sp^2$ hybridized.

Carbon atom $C_3$ is bonded to two carbon atoms via single bonds and two hydrogen atoms via single bonds. It forms $4$ sigma bonds and $0$ pi bonds. Thus, $C_3$ is $sp^3$ hybridized.

Therefore, the $C_2 - C_3$ bond is formed by the overlap of $sp^2$ and $sp^3$ hybridized orbitals, making it an $sp^2 - sp^3$ type bond.

Answer: $sp^2 - sp^3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the type of hybridization of carbon that is attached to the OH group, in benzylic alcohol?
questions.solution:
The structure of benzylic alcohol is $C_6H_5-CH_2-OH$.

The carbon atom attached to the $-OH$ group is bonded to one carbon atom of the benzene ring, two hydrogen atoms, and one oxygen atom.

Since it forms exactly four sigma bonds and has zero lone pairs, its steric number is $4$.

Therefore, the hybridization of this carbon atom is $sp^3$.

Answer: $sp^3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the different types of bonds present in quaternary ammonium salts.
questions.solution:
Quaternary ammonium salts have the general formula $R_4N^+ X^-$.

The bonds present within the alkyl or aryl groups ($R$) and three of the nitrogen-carbon bonds are covalent.

The fourth nitrogen-carbon bond is formed by the donation of the lone pair of electrons from the nitrogen atom to an electron-deficient carbon atom, which is a co-ordinate (dative) bond.

The electrostatic force of attraction between the complex quaternary ammonium cation ($R_4N^+$) and the counter anion ($X^-$) constitutes an ionic bond.

Thus, quaternary ammonium salts contain covalent, co-ordinate, and ionic bonds.

Answer: covalent, co-ordinate and ionic

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the shape of $\text{IF}_5$ molecule from the following options.
questions.solution:
The central atom is Iodine (I), which has $7$ valence electrons.

It forms $5$ single bonds with $5$ Fluorine (F) atoms.

Number of bond pairs = $5$

Number of lone pairs = $\dfrac{7 - 5}{2} = 1$

Total number of electron pairs = $5 + 1 = 6$

The hybridization of the central atom is $sp^3d^2$, which corresponds to an octahedral electron geometry.

Due to the presence of $5$ bond pairs and $1$ lone pair, the molecular shape is square pyramidal.

Answer: Square pyramidal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following forces is involved in dinitrogen?
questions.solution:
The dinitrogen molecule ($N_2$) consists of two identical nitrogen atoms with symmetrical electron distribution, making it nonpolar.

Dipole-dipole interaction requires permanent molecular dipoles. Dipole-induced dipole interaction involves a polar molecule inducing a dipole in a nonpolar molecule. Hydrogen bonding requires hydrogen attached to N, O, or F atoms. London dispersion forces arise from instantaneous electron fluctuations and operate in all molecular systems.

For nonpolar $N_2$, London dispersion forces constitute the only intermolecular interaction present.

The correct choice is $\boxed{C}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following molecules does not obey octet rule?
questions.solution:
The octet rule analysis proceeds by assessing the Lewis structure of each molecule, focusing on the central atom's electron count.

C$O_2$: The predicted structure is O=C=O. Carbon shares four bonds with oxygen, each oxygen retains two lone pairs, so oxygen has $2 + 3 \times 2 = 8$ electrons and carbon has $4 \times 2 = 8$ electrons—satisfying the octet rule.

CHCl_3$: Carbon forms single bonds with hydrogen and three chlorine atoms. Hydrogen has $2$ electrons from its bond, each chlorine has $1 \times 2 + 3 \times 2 = 8$ electrons, and carbon has $4 \times 2 = 8$ electrons—satisfying the octet rule.

ClF_3$: Chlorine forms three single bonds with fluorine atoms and bears two lone pairs. Each fluorine has $1 \times 2 + 3 \times 2 = 8$ electrons, but chlorine has $3 \times 2 + 2 \times 2 = 10$ electrons, exceeding the octet—violating the rule.

NH_3$: Nitrogen forms three single bonds with hydrogen atoms and holds one lone pair. Each hydrogen has $2$ electrons, nitrogen has $3 \times 2 + 2 = 8$ electrons—satisfying the octet rule.

Therefore, ClF_3$ does not obey the octet rule.

Final answer: $\boxed{C}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the bond order of $\mathrm{NO}^{+}$ion.
questions.solution:
The $\mathrm{NO}^{+}$ ion contains 14 electrons, with 7 from nitrogen and 8 from oxygen minus 1 due to the positive charge.

Its molecular orbital configuration follows the standard filling order for diatomic molecules: $(\sigma 1s)^2 (\sigma^* 1s)^2 (\sigma 2s)^2 (\sigma^* 2s)^2 (\pi 2p)^4 (\sigma 2p)^2$.

The bond order is calculated as half the difference between bonding and antibonding electrons. There are 10 bonding electrons ($\sigma 1s$, $\sigma 2s$, $\pi 2p$, and $\sigma 2p$) and 4 antibonding electrons ($\sigma^* 1s$ and $\sigma^* 2s$), giving $\frac{1}{2}(10 - 4) = 3$.

The bond order is $3$, corresponding to choice $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from the following molecules does not develop intermolecular hydrogen bonding?
questions.solution:
Intermolecular hydrogen bonding requires hydrogen atoms covalently bonded to highly electronegative atoms (F, O, or N) adjacent to atoms with lone electron pairs.

Water ($\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$) features hydrogen-oxygen bonds with oxygen lone pairs, enabling hydrogen bonding.

Ammonia ($\mathrm{NH}_3$) has hydrogen-nitrogen bonds with nitrogen lone pairs, facilitating hydrogen bonding.

Hydrogen fluoride (HF) contains hydrogen-fluorine bonds with fluorine lone pairs, supporting strong hydrogen bonding.

Bromine ($\mathrm{Br}_2$) lacks hydrogen atoms entirely and consists only of bromine-bromine covalent bonds, precluding hydrogen bonding entirely. Intermolecular forces are limited to London dispersion forces.

$\mathrm{Br}_2$ is therefore the only molecule among these that cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following molecules is square pyramidal?
questions.solution:
Molecular geometry determination using VSEPR theory:

For $\mathrm{XeF}_4$, xenon has four bonding pairs and two lone pairs, giving octahedral electron geometry and square planar molecular geometry.

For $\mathrm{XeF}_6$, xenon has six bonding pairs and one lone pair, resulting in pentagonal bipyramidal electron geometry and distorted octahedral molecular geometry.

For $\mathrm{XeOF}_4$, xenon has five bonding domains (four single bonds to fluorine and one double bond to oxygen) and one lone pair, yielding octahedral electron geometry and square pyramidal molecular geometry.

For $\mathrm{XeO}_3$, xenon has three bonding domains (double bonds to oxygen) and one lone pair, giving tetrahedral electron geometry and trigonal pyramidal molecular geometry.

The molecule with square pyramidal geometry is $\mathrm{XeOF}_4$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is correct decreasing order of bond length regarding $\mathrm{N}_2, \mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ ?
questions.solution:
Bond lengths decrease with increasing bond multiplicity and increase with larger atomic radii. The bond order and atomic size determine the bond length: $\mathrm{N}_2$ has a triple bond, $\mathrm{O}_2$ a double bond, and $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ a single bond.

$\mathrm{N}_2$: $\mathrm{N} \equiv \mathrm{N}$, bond length $\approx$ 109.8 pm
$\mathrm{O}_2$: $\mathrm{O} = \mathrm{O}$, bond length $\approx$ 121 pm
$\mathrm{Cl}_2$: $\mathrm{Cl} - \mathrm{Cl}$, bond length $\approx$ 199 pm

Since higher bond order corresponds to shorter bonds, and chlorine has the largest atomic radius, the order is $\mathrm{Cl}_2 \gt \mathrm{O}_2 \gt \mathrm{N}_2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The attractive interactions between cations and mobile electrons in metallic solid is called
questions.solution:
The attractive interactions between cations and mobile electrons define metallic bonding.

In metallic solids, metal atoms lose valence electrons to form cations, while delocalized electrons form a shared "sea" throughout the structure.

The electrostatic attraction between these positive metal ions and negative delocalized electrons constitutes the metallic bond, often described as the electron sea model.


Other bond types differ significantly: ionic bonding involves complete electron transfer between atoms, covalent bonding involves electron sharing between specific atoms, and weak dipole-dipole interactions occur between polar molecules rather than within metallic structures.


The correct classification is therefore $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

Molecular shapes are determined using Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion theory, analyzing bonding pairs and lone pairs around the central atom.

$\text{NH}_3$ has trigonal pyramidal geometry (steric number 4, 1 lone pair), while $\text{SO}_2$ is bent (steric number 3, 1 lone pair)—different shapes.

$\text{XeF}_4$ is square planar (steric number 6, 2 lone pairs), while $\text{SF}_4$ is see-saw (steric number 5, 1 lone pair)—different shapes.

$\text{PCl}_5$ is trigonal bipyramidal (steric number 5, 0 lone pairs), while $\text{BrF}_5$ is square pyramidal (steric number 6, 1 lone pair)—different shapes.

$\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{SCl}_2$ both possess tetrahedral electron geometry with two bonding pairs and two lone pairs, resulting in identical bent molecular geometries.

questions.q: Which of the following is more polar?
questions.solution:
Molecular polarity depends on bond electronegativity differences and molecular geometry, with the overall dipole moment determined by the vector sum of individual bond dipoles.

$\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{S}$ exhibits bent geometry with bond dipoles that do not cancel, yielding $\mu \approx 0.97 \text{ D}$.

$\mathrm{NH}_3$'s trigonal pyramidal structure and highly polar N-H bonds produce a large dipole moment of $\mu \approx 1.47 \text{ D}$, enhanced by the lone pair contribution.

For $\mathrm{NF}_3$, the opposing directions of the N-F bond dipoles and lone pair dipole partially cancel, resulting in $\mu \approx 0.23 \text{ D}$.

$\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ has asymmetric tetrahedral geometry with non-canceling dipoles, giving $\mu \approx 1.04 \text{ D}$.

Comparing values, $\mathrm{NH}_3$ possesses the largest dipole moment.

questions.solution:
Determining lone pairs on central atoms requires analyzing valence electrons and bonding structure. Compounds with analogous electron domains exhibit equal lone pair counts when their bonding patterns yield identical remaining electron pairs.

$\mathrm{BrF}_5$ and $\mathrm{XeF}_6$: Bromine (Group 17) has 7 valence electrons; bonding to 5 fluorine atoms uses 5 electrons, leaving 2 (1 lone pair). Xenon (Group 18) has 8 valence electrons; bonding to 6 fluorine atoms uses 6 electrons, leaving 2 (1 lone pair). Both thus have one lone pair.

$\mathrm{ICl}$ has 3 lone pairs on iodine (7 valence electrons minus 1 bonding electron), while $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}$ has 2 lone pairs on sulfur (6 valence electrons minus 2 bonding electrons).

$\mathrm{ClF}_3$ has 2 lone pairs on chlorine; $\mathrm{XeF}_2$ has 3 lone pairs on xenon.

$\mathrm{IF}_7$ has 0 lone pairs; $\mathrm{XeF}_4$ has 2 lone pairs.

Only $\mathrm{BrF}_5$ and $\mathrm{XeF}_6$ share an identical lone pair count.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{A}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds has high lattice enthalpy?
questions.solution:
Lattice enthalpy depends on ionic charge magnitude and the sum of ionic radii, quantified by the relation $\text{Lattice Enthalpy} \propto \frac{|q_1 q_2|}{r_+ + r_-}$.

Among LiCl, NaCl, BeF_2$, and CaCl_2$, compounds with doubly charged cations (Be$^{2+}$ or Ca$^{2+}$) exhibit higher lattice enthalpy due to increased charge product. BeF_2$ and CaCl_2$ both have charge product $|(+2) \times (-1)| = 2$, whereas LiCl and NaCl have charge product $1$.

Be$^{2+}$ ($\approx 27$ pm) is smaller than Ca$^{2+}$ ($\approx 100$ pm), and F$^-$ ($\approx 133$ pm) is smaller than Cl$^-$ ($\approx 181$ pm), resulting in a notably smaller sum of radii for BeF_2$ ($\approx 160$ pm) compared to CaCl_2$ ($\approx 281$ pm).

Approximating the proportionality: for BeF_2$, $\frac{2}{160} = \frac{1}{80}$; for LiCl, $\frac{1}{257}$. The value for BeF_2$ is significantly larger, confirming it has the highest lattice enthalpy.

The answer is $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

questions.solution:
Isomorphism occurs when substances share similar crystal structures and chemical compositions, enabling mixed crystal formation. Critical requirements include identical formula types, comparable ionic radii, and matching valencies among corresponding ions.

Calcite and aragonite ($\text{CaCO}_3$) are polymorphs with identical composition but differing trigonal versus orthorhombic structures, precluding isomorphism.

Similarly, $\alpha$-quartz and cristobalite ($\text{SiO}_2$) exhibit polymorphism with trigonal and cubic structures respectively, lacking structural consistency for isomorphism.

Diamond and fullerene represent carbon allotropes with fundamentally different tetrahedral network versus spherical cage architectures, disqualifying them from isomorphism.

Sodium nitrate ($\text{NaNO}_3$) and calcite ($\text{CaCO}_3$) demonstrate isomorphism through their shared trigonal structure,
1:1 cation:anion ratio,
comparable ionic radii ($\text{Na}^+$ 0.102 nm versus $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ 0.100 nm),
and geometrically similar planar triangular anions ($\text{NO}_3^-$ and $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$).
Despite valence differences, their structural and dimensional congruence supports isomorphism.

Sodium nitrate and calcium carbonate exhibit isomorphism.

questions.q: What different types of bonds are formed by chlorine with oxygen in perchloric acid?
questions.solution:
Perchloric acid structure: Chlorine acts as the central atom bonded to four oxygen atoms, with one oxygen also bonded to hydrogen.

Total valence electrons: H (1) + Cl (7) + 4×O (24) = 32.

Initial bonding uses 5 bonds (Cl-O and O-H), consuming 10 electrons.
Remaining 22 electrons distribute as lone pairs: terminal O-H oxygen receives 2 pairs, three Cl-O oxygens each receive 3 pairs.

Formal charges reveal instability: Cl (+3), three oxygens (-1) each. Minimizing charges by converting lone pairs to bonds yields the optimal structure.

Final configuration shows chlorine bonded via:
• One single bond to oxygen in O-H group
• Three double bonds to remaining oxygen atoms

$\text{FC}_{\text{Cl}} = 7 - 0 - \frac{1}{2}(2 + 3\times4) = 0$
$\text{FC}_{\text{O}} = 6 - 4 - \frac{1}{2}(4) = 0$ for double-bonded oxygens

Thus chlorine forms one single bond and three double bonds with oxygen.

Analysis of Molecular Geometry

To determine which species is not tetrahedral, the hybridization and VSEPR geometry of each molecule or ion are analyzed. A species with a steric number of 4 and no lone pairs on the central atom exhibits tetrahedral geometry.

For $\mathrm{CH}_4$, the central carbon atom has steric number 4 with $sp^3$ hybridization and tetrahedral geometry.

For $\mathrm{SF}_4$, the central sulfur atom has valence electrons = 6, bonding pairs = 4, and lone pairs = 1, giving steric number 5 and $sp^3d$ hybridization. The geometry is see-saw, not tetrahedral.

For $\mathrm{NH}_4^+$, the nitrogen central atom has steric number 4 with $sp^3$ hybridization and tetrahedral geometry, as the +1 charge results in no lone pairs.

For $\mathrm{SiCl}_4$, the silicon central atom has steric number 4 with $sp^3$ hybridization and tetrahedral geometry.

Thus, only $\mathrm{SF}_4$ does not have tetrahedral geometry.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is shape of $\mathrm{BrF}_5$ molecule?
questions.solution:
Using VSEPR theory, the shape of $\mathrm{BrF}_5$ is determined by its electron and molecular geometries.
Bromine contributes 7 valence electrons, and each fluorine contributes 7, for a total of $1 \times 7 + 5 \times 7 = 42$ valence electrons.

Five single bonds use $5 \times 2 = 10$ electrons.
The remaining $42 - 10 = 32$ electrons are allocated as lone pairs.
Each fluorine requires 6 electrons to complete its octet, using $5 \times 6 = 30$ electrons.
The final $32 - 30 = 2$ electrons form one lone pair on bromine.

Thus, bromine has 5 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair, for a steric number of $5 + 1 = 6$.

An octahedral electron geometry with one lone pair yields a square pyramidal molecular geometry.

Final answer: The shape is square pyramidal, corresponding to choice $\boxed{C}$.

questions.q: Which of the following molecules has a regular geometry as expected?
questions.solution:
A molecule exhibits a regular geometry when its molecular geometry aligns precisely with its electron geometry, which typically requires no lone pairs on the central atom. Applying VSEPR theory to the given options reveals the following.

For SiC$l_{4}$, silicon has a steric number of 4 (4 bonding pairs, 0 lone pairs), yielding a tetrahedral electron and molecular geometry—a regular arrangement.

In SF_{4}$, sulfur has a steric number of 5 (4 bonding pairs, 1 lone pair), resulting in a see-saw molecular geometry that distorts the trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry.

For BrF_{5}$, bromine has a steric number of 6 (5 bonding pairs, 1 lone pair), leading to a square pyramidal molecular geometry that deviates from octahedral electron geometry.

In XeF_{4}$, xenon has a steric number of 6 (4 bonding pairs, 2 lone pairs), producing a square planar molecular geometry. Though highly symmetric, it differs from the octahedral electron geometry due to the lone pairs.

SiCl_{4}$ is unambiguously regular, with no lone pairs and ideal symmetry, so the answer is $\boxed{A}$.

The energy of an orbital in an atom depends on both the principal quantum number \((n)\) and the azimuthal quantum number \((l)\). According to the general trend, for orbitals with different principal quantum numbers, the one with the lower \(n\) typically has lower energy. For orbitals with the same \(n\), the one with the lower \(l\) value will have lower energy.
To identify the orbital with the lowest energy from the given options, consider:
The principal quantum number (\(n\)):
\(\begin{aligned}
& \text {2p: } n=2 \\
& 3 \mathrm{~s}: n=3 \\
& 3 \mathrm{~d}: n=3 \\
& \text {4p: } n=4
\end{aligned}\)
The azimuthal quantum number \((l)\) values for the different orbitals are:
\(\begin{aligned}
& 2 \mathrm{p}: l=1 \\
& 3 \mathrm{~s}: l=0 \\
& 3 \mathrm{~d}: l=2 \\
& 4 \mathrm{p}: l=1
\end{aligned}\)
The energy order for orbitals generally increases with increasing values of \((n+l)\), and for orbitals with the same \((n+l)\) value, the one with the smaller \(n\) has the lower energy.
Calculating \((n+l)\) :
\(2 \mathrm{p}: 2+1=3\)
\(3 \mathrm{~s}: 3+0=3\)
3d: \(3+2=5\)
\(4 \mathrm{p}: 4+1=5\)
Among the options with the same \((n+l)\) value (\(2 p\) and \(3 s\)), \(2 p\) has the lower principal quantum number (\(n=2\) vs. \(n=3\)). Thus, the orbital with the lowest energy is:
Option A: 2p

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following species has highest bond energy?
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{O}_{2}^{2-}=K K^{\prime} \sigma 2 s^{2}, \sigma^{*} 2 s^{2}, \sigma 2 p_{z}^{2}, \pi 2 p_{x}^{2}, \pi 2 p_{y}^{2}\pi^{*} 2 p_{x}^{2}, \pi 2 p_{y}^{2}$
Bond order $=\frac{N_{b}-N_{a}}{2}=\frac{8-6}{2}=1$
(b) $\mathrm{O}_{2}^{+}=K K^{\prime} \sigma 2 s^{2}, \sigma^{*} 2 s^{2}, \sigma 2 p_{z}^{2}, \pi 2 p_{x}^{2}=\pi 2 p_{y}^{2}\pi^{\star} 2 p_{x}^{1}$
Bond order $=\frac{8-3}{2}=2.5$
(c) $\mathrm{O}_{2}^{-}=K K^{\prime} \sigma 2 s^{2}, \sigma^{\star} 2 s^{2}, \sigma 2 p_{z}^{2}, \pi 2 p_{x}^{2} \approx \pi 2 p_{y}^{2}\pi 2 p_{x}^{2} \approx \pi \cdot 2 p_{y}^{*}$
Bond order $=\frac{8-5}{2}=1.5$
(d) $\mathrm{O}_{2}=K K^{\prime} \sigma 2 s^{2}, \sigma^{\star} 2 s^{2}, \sigma 2 p_{z}^{2}, \pi 2 p_{x}^{2} \approx \pi 2 p_{y}^{2}\pi 2 p_{x}^{*} \approx \pi 2 p_{y}^{1}$
Bond order $=\frac{8-4}{2}=2$
: Bond energy $\propto \frac{1}{\text { Bond order }}\therefore \mathrm{O}_{2}^{2-}$ has highest bond energy.
